chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Hishām ibn Aḥmar, who said:

Abū al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام said to me, “Have you come to know of anyone from the people of al-Maghrib who has arrived?” I said, “No.” He said, “Rather, a man has arrived, so come with us.” Then he rode, and I rode with him until we came to the man. There was a man from the people of al-Madīnah with him, and he had slave girls. So I said to him, “Show them to us.” He showed us seven slave girls, and throughout all of that Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام was saying, “I have no need of her.”

Then he said, “Show them to us.” The man said, “I have nothing except a sick slave girl.” He said to him, “What harm is there for you in showing her?” But he refused him, so he left. Then on the next day he sent me and said, “Say to him: ‘What was your final price for her?’ Then when he says such-and-such, say: ‘I have taken her.’” So I went to him, and he said, “I did not want to reduce her from such-and-such and such-and-such.” So I said, “I have taken her.”

He said, “She is yours, but tell me: who was the man that was with you yesterday?” I said, “A man from Banī Hāshim.” He said, “From which branch of Banī Hāshim?” I said, “I have nothing more than this.” He said, “I will tell you about this young maidservant. I bought her from the farthest part of al-Maghrib. Then a woman from the People of the Book met me and said, ‘What is this young maidservant with you?’ I said, ‘I bought her for myself.’ She said, ‘It is not fitting that this one should be with the likes of you. This slave girl ought to be with the best of the people of the earth. She will not remain with him except a little while, until she bears from him a غلام such that none like him will be born in the east of the earth nor in its west.’”
He said: So I brought her to him, and she did not remain with him except a short while until she gave birth to al-Riḍā عليه السلام.

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ الْأَوَّلُ: Abū al-Ḥasan the First, referring here to the Imam who initiates the purchase
key_terms.أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ: the People of the Book, referring to a non-Muslim scriptural community
key_terms.الرِّضَا: Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام, whose birth is the conclusion of the report
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبِ: the western lands from which the slave girl was brought
key_terms.الْوَصِيفَةِ: a young maidservant or slave girl
key_terms.جَوَارٍ: female slave girls presented to the buyer
key_terms.رَقِيقٌ: bondservants or slave property shown for sale
key_terms.غُلَامًا: a boy or young son to be born from her

ai.seo_question: How does al-Kāfī narrate the circumstances of the mother and birth of Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates how Abū al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام acquired a slave girl whose destiny, as foretold by a woman from the People of the Book, was to be with the best of the people of the earth and to bear an unparalleled son. The report concludes that she gave birth to al-Riḍā عليه السلام, making the narration significant in the biographical tradition concerning the birth and special status of Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham Bin Ahmar who said,

‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1<sup>st</sup> said to me: ‘Do you know anyone from the people of Al-Maghreb (Morocco) to have arrived?’ I said, ‘No, but  a man has arrived (from somewhere)’. So we went, and he<sup>asws</sup> rode and I rode with him until we ended up to the man. But, there was thin man from the people of Al-Medina with him. So I said to him, ‘Display to us’. So he displayed seven slave girls to us, for each of that Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> was saying to the man from the people of Al-Medina: ‘There is no need for me with regards to her’.

Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Display to us’. So he said, ‘There is nothing with me except for a sick slave girl’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘What is it to you if you were to display her’. But he refused to him<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> left. Then he<sup>asws</sup> sent me the next day, and he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Say to him, ‘How much was your maximum price regarding her?’ So if he says, ‘Such and such’, so say, ‘I take her’. So I went over to him, but he said, ‘I would not have taken anything less than such and such’. So I said, ‘I have taken her’.

So he said, ‘She is yours, but, inform me, who was the man who was with you yesterday?’ So I said, ‘A man from the Clan of Hashim<sup>as</sup>’. He said, ‘From which son of Hashim<sup>as</sup>?’ So I said, ‘There is nothing more with me than this’. So he said, ‘I inform about this maid. I bought her from the outskirts of Al-Maghreb, and a woman from the People of the Book met me, and she said, ‘Who is this maid with you?’ I said, ‘I bought her for myself’. So she said, ‘It does not happen to be befitting that this one should be with the likes of you. This slave girl is such that it is befitting that she happens to be with the best of the people of the earth. So she would not remain with him except for a little until she would be Blessed with a boy from him such that the like of him has neither been born in the east nor its west.
He (the narrator) said, ‘So I went over to him<sup>asws</sup> with her, and she did not remain with him<sup>asws</sup> except for a little until she was Blessed Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: Abu al-Hassan al-Rida (a.s.) was born in the year the one hundred forty eight AH. He passed away in the month of Safar in the year two hundred and three at the age of fifty-five. All the views about this date are not the same but it is more accurate, if Allah would so will. He died in Tus in the town called Sanabad, that is within the reach of human voice from Nawqan. He was buried there.

Al-Ma’mun had summoned him from Madina to Marw via Basra to Persia. When al-Ma’mun left for Baghdad he took The Imam (a.s.) he passed away in this town. His mother was ’Umm Walad called ’Umm al-Banin.
